Operator: Good day, and welcome to the CyberFortress Inc. Q3 FY2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. Instructions for joining the question and answer session will be given at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss CyberFortress Inc.'s results for the third quarter of fiscal year 2024. With me on today's call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; and Dr. Lena Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed description of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good afternoon, everyone. Thank you for joining us. CyberFortress had a strong Q3, driven by continued demand for our cybersecurity solutions and our commitment to innovation. We are seeing increased adoption of our CyberFortress One platform, which is helping organizations better protect themselves against increasingly sophisticated cyber threats.

Our focus remains on four key areas: expanding our cohort of high-value customers with ARR over $100K, accelerating platform adoption over fragmented point products, delivering robust ARR growth both quarter-over-quarter and year-over-year, and rolling out game-changing product and feature launches that address the evolving threat landscape.

Let me touch briefly on those recent innovations before handing over to Mike. We've launched several critical enhancements that are resonating strongly with customers. Our NexusGuard Sentinel AI, a next-gen EDR platform powered by multimodal large language models and behavioral analytics, has automated much of the alert triage process, slashing MTTR dramatically while providing explainable AI for trust and accuracy. We've also introduced QuantumShield, our post-quantum cryptography suite with hybrid key exchange using standards like Kyber and Dilithium, perfectly timed ahead of NIST finalizations to protect against emerging quantum risks. And Apex SASE 2.0 rounds it out, consolidating SD-WAN, ZTNA, and CASB with inline GenAI sandboxing for edge-secured environments. These have already driven significant new ARR and positioned us ahead of the curve in AI-first, zero-trust defenses.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Mike Thompson to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Mike Thompson: Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we had a strong Q3. Revenue for the quarter was $385 million, representing a 32% increase year-over-year. This growth was driven by strong performance across all of our product lines. Our gross margin was 87%, and our operating expenses were $220 million. Net income for the quarter was $65 million, or $0.85 per share.

Before we dive deeper, let me highlight one of our key leading indicators for sustained growth: the number of customers generating over $100K in Annual Recurring Revenue, or ARR. This cohort represents our largest, most strategic enterprise accounts—those that have fully embraced our CyberFortress One Unified Threat Management platform, including our AI-powered Next-Gen Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), Secure Access Service Edge (SASE), and Cloud Workload Protection (CWP) modules. These are the logos driving the majority of our dollar-based net retention, or NRR, which came in at 128% this quarter.

As of the end of Q3, we now have 528 customers with ARR exceeding $100K. That's a sequential increase of 42 customers, or 9% quarter-over-quarter, and a robust 24% year-over-year growth from the 425 we reported this time last year. To put this in context, these high-value customers account for approximately 72% of our total ARR of $1.42 billion, up from 68% a year ago, underscoring our land-and-expand model. The average ARR per customer in this group has also expanded to $347K, reflecting strong upsell and cross-sell into our full platform stack—particularly our Autonomous XDR solution, which correlates threats across endpoints, networks, and cloud environments with sub-millisecond latency.

This growth isn't accidental; it's the direct result of several technical and go-to-market initiatives tailored to the cybersecurity landscape. First, our HyperShield AI engine, launched in Q1, has been a game-changer. It leverages generative AI for predictive threat hunting, reducing mean time to detect (MTTD) by 65% and mean time to respond (MTTR) by 78% in beta deployments. We've seen 37 new $100K+ logos this quarter specifically citing HyperShield integrations with incumbent tools like Splunk Enterprise Security and Microsoft Sentinel, allowing seamless data lake federation without rip-and-replace. In fact, 62% of expansions in this cohort involved bundling EDR with our SASE fabric, capitalizing on the post-Okta breach momentum where enterprises are prioritizing zero-trust network access (ZTNA) over legacy VPNs.

Regionally, the story is equally compelling. North America remains our powerhouse, contributing 68% of these customers—up 18% YoY—with mega-deals in financial services and healthcare. Think wins against Palo Alto's Prisma suite and Zscaler's Zero Trust Exchange, where we displaced them on price-performance for hybrid workloads. A prime example: a top-5 U.S. bank expanded from $150K endpoint ARR to $850K total platform ARR, driven by our compliance-ready controls for PCI-DSS 4.0 and NIST 800-53 Rev 5. EMEA grew even faster at 32% YoY, now 22% of the cohort, fueled by GDPR enforcement and the NIS2 Directive. We added 12 new logos here, including a European automotive OEM migrating from CrowdStrike Falcon due to our superior cloud-native CWP for OT/IoT convergence amid rising supply chain attacks like those seen in the Clop ransomware campaigns targeting Ivanti and MOVEit.

APAC is our emerging bright spot, up 45% YoY to 10% of the total, with Japan and Australia leading. Regulatory tailwinds like Japan's My Number Act and Australia's Essential Eight maturation have accelerated adoption. We secured eight expansions quarter-over-quarter, including a telco giant in Singapore upsell to $450K ARR for our Deception-as-a-Service module, which uses honeypots and behavioral analytics to counter APT41-style nation-state threats.

Strategically, these metrics validate our platformization thesis in a market where point solutions are commoditizing. Gartner pegs the endpoint security market at $12.5B in 2024, growing to $18B by 2028, but the real opportunity is in the $45B+ SASE/SSO convergence space. Our NRR of 128%—with 45% gross retention and 83% expansion—beats the industry average of 110-115% because we're not just selling modules; we're embedding via our CyberGraph API ecosystem. Partnerships with AWS (via Marketplace private offers) and Azure Sentinel have driven 25% of Q3 wins, as customers consolidate vendors amid economic headwinds—IT budgets are flat, but cyber spend is up 15% per IDC.

Looking ahead, we expect this cohort to hit 580 by year-end, implying 22% YoY growth, as our Q4 pipeline shows 3.2x coverage on $100K+ deals. Key catalysts include the GA of HyperShield 2.0 with quantum-resistant cryptography for post-quantum threats, and our push into federal with FedRAMP High authorization, targeting DISA STIG compliance. We've also seen a 15% uptick in multi-year contracts at 40%+ ACV uplift, insulating us from churn in a volatile macro where ransomware payouts hit $1.1B in H1 per Chainalysis.

Shifting to another critical growth driver: the accelerating shift in customer preference from fragmented point products to our integrated CyberFortress One platform. This transition is not just a trend—it's a structural change in the cybersecurity landscape, driven by escalating threats, regulatory pressures, and the operational realities of managing sprawling security stacks.

For Q3, our platform adoption rate—defined as the percentage of total ARR derived from customers deploying three or more modules within the CyberFortress One ecosystem—reached 68% of total ARR, up from 52% a year ago and 61% in Q2. This represents a 31% YoY increase in platform-derived ARR, growing to $428 million from $327 million. In contrast, point product ARR—standalone deployments of single modules like our legacy Endpoint Protection or isolated Cloud Workload Protection—shrank to 32% of total ARR, down from 48% YoY, clocking in at $212 million with just 2% YoY growth. This bifurcation underscores the maturity of our platform strategy: platforms now contribute 85% of new bookings, up from 72% last year.

To put this in perspective, we added 147 net new platform customers in Q3, a 24% YoY increase, bringing our total platform customer base to 2,340—enterprises with 5,000+ employees predominantly. Our Net Revenue Retention (NRR) for platform customers hit 128%, fueled by average module expansion of 4.2 modules per customer, compared to a stagnant 98% NRR for point product holdouts. Annual Contract Value (ACV) for platform deals averaged $1.47 million, 3.2x higher than point products at $460,000. Remaining Performance Obligations (RPO) for platforms surged 52% YoY to $2.1 billion, signaling multi-year commitments and reduced churn risk.

Why is this happening now? The cybersecurity market is at an inflection point. According to Gartner's latest Magic Quadrant for Endpoint Protection Platforms, over 70% of enterprises report "vendor sprawl" as their top pain point, with teams juggling 50+ point solutions on average—think Symantec endpoints, FireEye network detection, or standalone CASBs like Netskope. This leads to alert fatigue (up 40% per IDC surveys post-Log4j), siloed data, and skills gaps amid a global shortage of 3.5 million cybersecurity professionals (per Cybersecurity Ventures). Our platform counters this with XDR-orchestrated intelligence: unified data lakes ingesting 15 petabytes daily across EDR, NDR, CWPP, SSPM, and CNAPP modules, powered by our GenAI-driven HyperShield AI engine for autonomous threat hunting and response.

Technically, we've invested heavily in interoperability. Q3 saw the GA of our Zero-Trust Fabric integration, enabling seamless policy enforcement across on-prem, hybrid, and multi-cloud environments—AWS, Azure, GCP. Early adopters, like a Fortune 50 financial services client, reduced mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) from 48 hours to under 2 hours, consolidating eight point tools (including Palo Alto's Prisma Access and CrowdStrike's Falcon Insight) into our stack. We've also rolled out SOAR-native automation workflows, with uptake at 62% among platform users, slashing manual triage by 75%. These initiatives aren't hype; they're battle-tested against real-world threats like the Change Healthcare ransomware or recent Ivanti zero-days.

Regionally, North America remains our powerhouse, accounting for 64% of platform ARR with 42% YoY growth, propelled by CIS Controls v8 compliance and SEC cyber disclosure rules. We've seen hyperscalers like a major cloud provider expand from point EDR to full-stack platform, adding $28 million in upsell. EMEA grew 36% YoY to 22% of platform ARR, boosted by NIS2 Directive mandates—our DACH region (Germany, Austria, Switzerland) hit 91% adoption rate among existing customers, outpacing the EU average. APAC, at 10% of ARR, accelerated to 28% YoY growth despite headwinds; Singapore and Japan lead with platform penetration at 55%, driven by PDPA and My Number Act alignments, though China's data sovereignty rules cap us at point products for now—we're piloting localized instances via our Shanghai JV. LatAm and emerging markets are nascent but promising, with 45% QoQ platform bookings growth tied to Brazil's LGPD enforcement.

Strategically, this platform flywheel enhances our moat. Gross margins on platform revenue hit 89%, versus 82% for points, thanks to shared R&D leverage—we're allocating 28% of opex to AI/ML enhancements, yielding 35% faster feature velocity. Compared to peers, our platform module attach rate of 4.2x edges CrowdStrike's 3.8x (per their Q2 call) and crushes Zscaler's zero-trust niche at 2.1x expansions. SentinelOne's point-heavy mix explains their slower NRR; we're pulling ahead by addressing the "platformization" wave Gartner predicts will capture 65% of the $85 billion EDR/XDR market by 2027.

Looking forward, we guide Q4 platform adoption to 72-74% of ARR, with full-year FY2024 at 67%. Expect continued point product rationalization: we're offering 20% migration credits for legacy tools, targeting 15% YoY contraction in that segment. Risks? Macro headwinds could slow deals, but our dollar-based net expansion of 122% and 107% bookings growth provide buffer. Ultimately, as breaches like Okta's or MOVEit prove, point products are yesterday's news—platforms are the resilience imperative.

Now, turning to our Annual Recurring Revenue, or ARR, performance, which remains the cornerstone of our SaaS-driven cybersecurity model. ARR ended the quarter at $1.42 billion, reflecting robust 18% quarter-over-quarter (QoQ) growth from $1.20 billion at the end of Q2, and an exceptional 42% year-over-year (YoY) growth from $1.0 billion in Q3 FY2023. These figures underscore our execution in a market where global cybersecurity spending is projected to exceed $200 billion in 2024, per Gartner, fueled by escalating ransomware attacks—up 30% YoY according to our threat intelligence data—and the shift to zero-trust architectures amid rising nation-state threats like those from APT41 and Lazarus Group.

Breaking this down by key drivers, new logo acquisitions contributed approximately 45% of our QoQ ARR expansion, with 320 net new customers added, bringing our total customer count to over 4,200. This included several hyperscale wins, such as a $15 million ACV deal with a top-5 cloud provider for our CyberFortress XDR platform—our extended detection and response solution that integrates seamlessly with SIEM tools like Splunk and Elastic. Average ACV for these new enterprise logos came in at $2.8 million, up 12% QoQ, reflecting a preference for our multi-year contracts, which now represent 65% of bookings.

Expansions and upsells drove the remaining 55% of growth, with our dollar-based net retention rate—or NDR—hitting a record 128%, comparable to CrowdStrike's recent quarters. Customers are rapidly adopting our full-stack portfolio: our SASE platform, CyberFortress Secure Access, saw 55% YoY ARR growth to $420 million, propelled by integrations with SD-WAN providers like VMware's VeloCloud. Similarly, endpoint protection ARR surged 60% YoY to $510 million, benefiting from AI-powered behavioral analytics that reduced false positives by 40% in our latest agentless deployment model.

Regionally, the Americas led with 50% YoY ARR growth to $780 million, driven by federal sector wins under CMMC 2.0 compliance—think DoD primes like Lockheed Martin analogs expanding their footprints. EMEA grew 38% YoY to $320 million, despite macro headwinds, thanks to DORA regulation tailwinds and a landmark €50 million deal with a European bank for our cloud-native NGFW, directly competing with Palo Alto's Prisma Access. APAC was our fastest grower at 55% YoY to $150 million, with strong traction in Japan and Australia amid PDPA and APRA CPS 234 mandates; we closed 15 deals over $5 million ACV, including a telco giant mirroring NTT's scale.

Strategically, these results stem from three initiatives. One, our $250 million R&D investment in GenAI threat hunting—launched in Q1—which has boosted detection of zero-day exploits like those in the recent MOVEit vulnerability by 35%, per our MITRE ATT&CK evaluations. Two, the acquisition of ThreatLynx last quarter added $45 million in ARR from deception tech, accelerating our move into autonomous SOCs. Three, our channel-first GTM, with partners like Deloitte and Accenture contributing 55% of bookings, has expanded our addressable market into mid-market via co-sell motions.

Looking ahead, we expect Q4 ARR growth of 16-18% QoQ, with FY2024 full-year guidance raised to 40-42% YoY, assuming no material escalation in supply chain disruptions like those from the Change Healthcare breach. Our rule of 70—combining 42% growth and 28% FCF margin—positions us for continued share gains in a fragmented market where leaders like Zscaler and SentinelOne are setting the pace.

We are confident that we are well-positioned to continue to drive growth and profitability in the years to come.

Operator, we are now ready to open the call for questions.

Operator: Instructions for the question and answer session. At this time, we will open the line for questions. To ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, please press star then two. Today's first question comes from Ben Smith with Goldman Sachs.

Ben Smith: Thanks, and congrats on the strong quarter. Mike, could you expand on the drivers behind the $100K+ customer cohort growth, particularly in EMEA and APAC, and how that ties into your NRR?

Mike Thompson: Thanks, Ben. Absolutely, as I detailed earlier, that cohort grew to 528, with EMEA up 32% YoY thanks to NIS2 and GDPR, adding logos like that automotive OEM shifting from CrowdStrike for better OT/IoT protection amid Clop-style attacks. APAC jumped 45% on regs like My Number, with expansions like the Singapore telco to $450K on Deception-as-a-Service against APT41. This directly fuels our 128% NRR, with expansions averaging 83% from cross-sells into XDR and SASE—strong validation of our platform strategy.

Operator: Next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen: Great, thanks. Mike, on platform adoption hitting 68%, how are you seeing the competitive dynamics play out there, especially versus CrowdStrike and Zscaler, and any update on migration incentives?

Mike Thompson: Lisa, thanks for the question. Platform ARR now dominates at 68%, with 4.2x module attach outpacing CrowdStrike's 3.8x and Zscaler's narrower focus. Customers are fleeing sprawl—70% cite it per Gartner—and our Zero-Trust Fabric and SOAR workflows are winning consolidations, like that Fortune 50 bank ditching eight tools. We're pushing 20% credits for legacy migrations, expecting point products to contract 15% YoY as platforms hit 72-74% in Q4.

Operator: Next question comes from Raj Patel with JPMorgan.

Raj Patel: Hi, team. Dr. Patel, can you speak to the technical differentiators in HyperShield AI and how it's performing against benchmarks like MITRE ATT&CK, especially post recent launches?

Dr. Lena Patel: Thanks, Raj. HyperShield, building on Sentinel AI, uses GenAI for predictive hunting with XAI to ensure 98% accuracy on APT sims, cutting MTTD 65% and MTTR 78%. In MITRE evals, we've boosted zero-day detection 35% versus MOVEit exploits. QuantumShield adds FIPS-compliant post-quantum keys with <1ms latency, and Apex SASE 2.0's sandboxing hits 99.2% on prompt injections. These are embedding via CyberGraph APIs, driving 128% net expansion.

Operator: Next question comes from Emma Rodriguez with Barclays.

Emma Rodriguez: Thanks. Alex, with ARR at $1.42B and 42% YoY growth, how does the regional mix evolution impact your FY24 guidance, and any thoughts on federal push?

Alex Rivera: Emma, great question. Americas at 50% growth to $780M on CMMC, EMEA 38% on DORA with that €50M bank win, APAC 55% on PDPA/APRA—pipeline's 3.2x covered. Federal's key with FedRAMP High incoming, mirroring DoD expansions. This supports raised FY24 ARR guide of 40-42% YoY, with launches like Sentinel AI scaling to $500M run-rate, contributing 35-40% to Q4 growth amid 16% industry CAGR.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, everyone, for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees, customers, and partners for their continued support. We are excited about the opportunities ahead and are confident that we can continue to deliver strong results.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you for joining us today. This concludes our call. You may now disconnect.
